title: MCP architecture
finding: MCP separates host, client and server responsibilities; the host controls cross-server context and security boundaries.
limit: Protocol architecture does not implement an entire harness, workflow policy or safe deployment.

title: MCP security best practices
locator: Confused deputy; token passthrough; SSRF; session/security considerations
finding: The guidance identifies audience-validation/token-passthrough and network/session attack risks in MCP deployments.
limit: Guidance and protocol rules are not evidence that a particular deployment enforces them; authorization details depend on the transport/version.

title: OpenAI function calling
locator: Function-calling flow; tool calls and tool outputs
finding: Function calling separates model-requested operations from application execution and subsequent tool-result input.
limit: A generated call or schema-valid argument is not authorization, successful execution or an observed business outcome.

title: OpenAI conversation state
finding: Applications can carry conversation state explicitly or use supported service-managed state mechanisms.
limit: Specific chaining/retention behavior is provider/API-specific; saved history is not automatically a task database or universal context guarantee.

title: OpenAI compaction
finding: The current guide distinguishes server-side and standalone compaction and describes opaque encrypted carry-forward items with route-specific continuation handling.
limit: Opaque items are not editable semantic-memory notes. Follow the chosen API's output/chaining contract; do not generalize manual pruning across routes.

title: OpenAI prompt caching
locator: Reusable rendered prefix; cache location; compaction/cache interaction
finding: Prompt caching reuses eligible model computation for a matching rendered prefix. Compaction may change that prefix.
limit: Caching is not durable knowledge storage or a larger context window. Rates, thresholds, retention and support are model/account/version-dependent and are not fixed recommendations here.

title: OpenAI agents overview
locator: Agents API / Agents SDK / Responses comparison
finding: The guide distinguishes managed harness infrastructure, an application-controlled SDK runner and lower-level model/tool integration.
limit: The guide describes specific OpenAI products; these layers are comparison examples, not a selection of our provider or runtime.

title: OpenAI: Building Reliable Agents with Memory and Compaction
locator: Compaction versus memory; reviewed investigation artifacts
finding: The synthetic cookbook separates current-run continuity, cross-run workflow memory and reviewed output artifacts.
limit: A teaching example does not prove every summarized fact is preserved or establish healthcare validity/our project performance.

title: Anthropic: Effective context engineering for AI agents
locator: Context curation; compaction; structured notes; sub-agent architectures
finding: Describes selective context assembly, compaction, external notes and focused sub-agent contexts as techniques for finite-context work.
limit: Engineering guidance is not a universal optimal context policy; tradeoffs must be evaluated on actual tasks.

title: Anthropic: Effective harnesses for long-running agents
locator: Initializer/incremental worker; progress artifacts; testing; future work
finding: Reports a long-running coding workflow using durable progress/requirements artifacts and incremental verified work across sessions.
limit: The article presents one coding-oriented approach and explicitly leaves broader generalization and team structure open. Its filenames/architecture are not requirements for our system.

title: Anthropic: Writing effective tools for agents
locator: Purpose/namespacing; meaningful bounded responses; tool evaluation
finding: Discusses agent-facing tool purpose, descriptions, response content and evaluation instead of merely exposing every low-level endpoint.
limit: Reported ergonomic/performance observations are task/model-dependent; preserve required identifiers and authoritative state in our own contracts.

title: Anthropic: Code execution with MCP
locator: Programmatic tool access; filtering intermediate results; execution environment
finding: Describes executing orchestration code to discover/call tools and filter intermediate data before it enters model context.
limit: A code-execution design adds a runtime/security boundary and is an alternative to direct tool calls, not a required harness ingredient.

title: Anthropic: Advanced tool use
locator: Tool search; programmatic tool calling; usage examples
finding: Describes tool discovery and programmatic use patterns that reduce the need to load every schema/intermediate result into active context.
limit: Feature availability and provider API details are product-specific; a generic harness needs adapter/capability negotiation rather than assuming all providers support them.

title: Anthropic: Demystifying evals for AI agents
locator: Trials, tasks, graders and traces; agent evaluation practices
finding: Distinguishes evaluating task outcomes from inspecting trajectories and discusses the practical difficulty of evaluating stochastic tool-using systems.
limit: It does not supply our evaluation set or establish any local pass rate. Our test proposals and executed synthetic checks must remain separate.

title: AWS Builders' Library: Making retries safe with idempotent APIs
locator: Unique caller-provided request identifier; atomic mutation/dedupe; same key/different intent; retention
finding: Describes request-identity contracts and atomic deduplication with the associated mutation, including parameter mismatch and retention considerations.
limit: This applies where the actual receiving service supports the contract. A local checkpoint cannot make an arbitrary external service execute exactly once.

title: SQLite transactional guarantees
locator: Atomic, consistent, isolated and durable transactions
finding: Documents transactional behavior for SQLite storage.
limit: Storage guarantees depend on the documented platform/filesystem/settings assumptions and do not atomically include unrelated remote services.

title: SQLite write-ahead logging
finding: Describes WAL readers/writer concurrency, checkpoints and deployment restrictions.
limit: WAL is not a guarantee of unlimited concurrent writers or a substitute for application-level ownership, supported filesystem behavior and backups.

title: Stripe idempotent requests
locator: Idempotency keys; v1/v2 response semantics; retention and parameter validation
finding: Provides a concrete service-specific example of request keys, response replay and version-sensitive retry behavior.
limit: Do not assume every tool uses Stripe's rules, retention period or semantics; this research does not perform any Stripe call.
